name: Balbach Teaching Dimension of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, the ordinary minimum teaching size is zero, and the empty sample retains exactly the sole target at every Balbach step. For $n\ge2$, each ordinary minimum size is one, because the positive example isolates its singleton while the empty sample is consistent with all targets. At the all-one size vector these same positive samples survive the filter and isolate their targets; the empty sample retains all targets. Thus the all-one vector is fixed and the Balbach dimension is one.
